newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban report taking strategic pass.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban report taking strategic pass.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia on Monday captured the strategic Shibber Pass in Bamiyan province northwest of the capital Kabul, the official Voice of Shariat radio said.

The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, said the Taleban forces seized the pass, regarded as a gateway to northern and central Afghanistan, from opposition forces after a day-long offensive and were moving towards the northern province of Baghlan.
Earlier, a Taleban spokesman in Kabul said the militia had recaptured a number of positions from the opposition alliance in central Afghanistan.
Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said the fighting took place in Lolenj district in the Ghorband valley some 130 km (80 miles), northwest of Kabul.
The Ghorband valley leads up to the Shibber Pass, which lies across one of the main routes to the opposition-held north of Afghanistan.
